correctness.rationale: Direct differentiation yields the exact forced Volterra coboundary; integrated log predator and log prey identities fix mean N and express mean predator deficit as forcing–prey covariance. A periodic average of the Volterra derivative converts covariance into a strictly positive forcing-weighted prey variance for any positive nonconstant forcing. The unforced Jacobian is Hurwitz for all admissible parameters, hence the local period map has a unique attracting analytic fixed point for small harmonic forcing at each fixed positive frequency. Its resolvent gives the quadratic coefficient; a half-period forcing sign-change excludes odd terms, and differentiation with z=omega² gives the unique global coefficient maximum. SymPy verified both key algebraic identities; a separate SciPy shooting/quadrature program tested 16 positive coexistence solutions. Scope explicitly excludes threshold crossings and does not infer universal proof from numerical examples.

value.rationale: The motivating threshold-tipping paper studies how forcing frequency changes extinction risk through resonant amplitude; a meaningful complementary observable is chronic predator population mean while the system stays in coexistence. The theorem gives an exact, all-waveform, all-amplitude sign restriction and quantitative variance/covariance identity for every positive locked state, not just a parameter slice. The weak-forcing coefficient supplies a sharp, universal, dimensionless peak magnitude and a unique optimizing frequency distinct from the free damped oscillation frequency. It is directly useful as a benchmark for abundance responses and is neither a mere restatement of the original extrema plots nor a numerically fitted correction. Limits and nonexistence claims are not overstated.
